rows.note: Explicitly a deformed gas tank. Teacher is right, gold too general.
Engine surge causing a driveline clunk / transmission harshness -- both explicitly named and causally linked. Gold has no support.

REVISED after 5/5 models independently chose a brake label and pulling the FULL (untruncated) narrative: my original read was cut off by the 1400-char preview before the actual incident -- 'my brakes completely failed' at a stop sign, later confirmed by GM as a known issue with an extended warranty. This is a real, confirmed brake failure (the earlier transmission saga is a separate, prior repair). Gold and teacher were both right; my adjudication working from truncated text was wrong. Brake subtype not distinguishable per B21.
Backup camera glitching/going black -- clean match. Teacher is right.
Diagnosed root cause is a crankshaft tone wheel (an engine-internal part), but the actual recall remedy is a PCM software flash (electrical). Both framings are defensible.
Gas cap indicator, gasoline smell, cited Audi fuel-pump recalls. Teacher is right, gold too general.
Despite an undiagnosed mess of parts swaps, the vehicle's own repeated dashboard message is 'FUEL SYSTEM MALFUNCTION' -- its own diagnostic points to the fuel system. Teacher is right.
Standalone A/C condenser leak causing carpet mold, recurring despite a TSB fix -- matches the standalone-AC-unit EQUIPMENT convention. Not a structural issue. Gold is right.
Text explicitly names 'a dangerous faulty hydraulic control unit (and ABS system)' -- confirms the hydraulic subtype directly, no air-brake evidence on this pickup.

Two explicitly quoted recall campaigns -- '(SUSPENSION:REAR:AXLE...)' and '(STRUCTURE: FRAME AND MEMBERS...)' -- and an independent mechanic separately confirmed the sub-frame itself was compromised. Both are genuinely correct.

Explicit 'Transmission failure' warning message and a gear shifter that won't engage Drive point clearly to POWER TRAIN; smoke under the hood could also relate to the quoted fuel-system recall. Plain ENGINE (gold) has no direct support.
Overdrive light, failure to shift, both 4WD motors replaced, told it needs a new transmission -- all drivetrain components, nothing aftermarket. Teacher is right, gold makes no sense here.

The confirmed, specific, recall-matched part is the coolant outlet Y-pipe; the brake mention is vague and the complainant admits uncertainty ('I think there may have been a recall'). Teacher is right.

A dozen simultaneous warning messages cascading across every vehicle system -- a total electronic malfunction, of which the headlight mention (gold) is one trivial detail among many. Teacher is right.
Daily dashboard electrical heat and repeated electrical-component replacements are the primary, most-detailed complaint; no coolant/overheating symptom exists to support gold. Teacher is right.
The narrative never states what the recall is even for -- zero identifying information in the text itself. Judged strictly from the text, teacher is right.
Both an inexplicable lateral airbag deployment and a drive shaft cracked in half are explicitly described as part of the same incident. Genuinely dual.
Three explicit, individually named failures in one crash: brakes failed, forward-collision warning didn't activate, and airbags didn't deploy. Genuinely can't be reduced to one.
Three fuel pump replacements in two months on a gas Ford -- a specific, repeated, named component. Teacher is right, gold too conservative.
Brakes and drivetrain are named with exactly equal weight ('4 times' each) -- genuinely can't prefer one system over the other from this terse text.
Two distinct, explicitly described, ongoing issues: an acceleration-only rattling noise (engine/mechanical) and a separate occasional false airbag-sensor trigger.
The core, most safety-relevant symptom is getting stuck in 1st gear and failing to shift out -- a transmission fault, not an engine defect. Teacher is right.

A sprawling list of a dozen unrelated minor defects across the whole truck, with no single primary complaint -- keeping the two most safety-relevant, repeated symptoms (a wheel cover coming off, and pulling/grinding under braking).

Headlights went out (the stated symptom) but the diagnosed cause is the Totally Integrated Power Module, a general electrical control module that also affects other systems in these trucks (as in case 1453167). Both are defensible.
Explicitly quotes the matching recall category '(VISIBILITY)' for the same confirmed failure mechanism on a later model year. Gold is right, teacher missed the quoted campaign.
A/C condenser fan failure with no overheating/coolant symptom -- matches the standalone-AC-unit EQUIPMENT convention. Gold is right, teacher reflects the pre-update convention.
Multiple distinct false ADAS activations described: a false collision-sensor slowdown and separate single-wheel traction-control events. No cruise/accelerator issue (gold) is actually described.
Premature pad/rotor wear alone, no fluid/pedal/master-cylinder detail to confirm the hydraulic subtype specifically.
Tread separated from the sidewall -- a textbook tire failure, no wheel/rim damage described. Teacher is right, gold is wrong.
Windshield cracked by a pebble -- no wiper involvement at all. Teacher is right, gold misapplied the wiper subtype.

Explicitly says every electrical component was checked (connections, batteries, starters, alternators, fuses) and nothing was found -- an exhaustive, fruitless electrical investigation, and no engine-mechanical symptom either. Neither original answer is confirmed by the text.

A blown head gasket with heavy white smoke is the same genuinely dual engine/cooling part as 1476775 -- and the white-smoke detail here is an even stronger coolant-burning signal. Gold's UNKNOWN OR OTHER doesn't fit since a specific part is clearly named.
A collapsing/crushing rear bucket seat is a named seat-mechanism defect. Teacher is right, gold too conservative.
Spontaneous sunroof glass shattering while closed -- matches the established convention that sunroof-glass failures are VISIBILITY, not structural. Gold is right.

Both a specific, repeatedly diagnosed brake issue (master cylinder replaced 3x) and a severe, separately remediated electrical cascade (entire electrical system replaced) are described in detail. Gold's STRUCTURE has no support at all.
Dashboard glare on the windshield obstructing view -- no wiper involvement. Teacher is right.
An unintended acceleration surge into a planter box -- classic pedal-sensitivity complaint. Gold's STRUCTURE has no support (the planter box isn't part of the vehicle). Teacher is right.
'ICCU failure' -- the same EV charging-control-unit failure as 1966802, which is the rare HYBRID PROPULSION SYSTEM category. Neither original answer is right.
'Shuts off without warning' with zero named component -- fits UNKNOWN OR OTHER's own definition exactly. Teacher is right.

REVISED after 5/5 models independently chose COMMUNICATION: I originally missed that GPS/navigation is explicitly covered by the COMMUNICATION rare category ('infotainment, telematics'). The root complaint (GPS shows wrong location, nav 'rendered useless') is a real, specific, well-described telematics defect -- not FORWARD COLLISION AVOIDANCE (no sensor/AEB defect described) and not UNKNOWN OR OTHER (a specific system IS named).
